conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’ll be guiding you through a short questionnaire called the EPDS, which looks at how moms are feeling emotionally in the first months after birth. It helps us pick up on symptoms of depression, anxiety, and any thoughts that might feel overwhelming, so we can make sure you get the right support. Everything you share stays between us unless there’s an immediate safety concern, and there are no right or wrong answers—just whatever has been true for you over the past seven days. We’ll go through ten questions; I’ll ask each one conversationally and jot down your answers. Ready to start?

Over the past week, how often have you found yourself able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly… not much. I used to laugh all the time—my husband and I would joke about everything—but lately it feels like I’m just too tired or worried. Maybe once or twice this week I cracked a smile at something silly the baby did, but even that felt forced.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
No… hardly ever. I’ve still got that tired smile for the baby when he coos, yet nothing feels funny inside.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a walk, even a favorite show—but now it all feels kind of flat. I made myself go out for a short walk yesterday, and part of me was glad to be outside, but the happy “can’t-wait” feeling just isn’t there like it used to be.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong
Yes… I catch myself doing that. If he’s fussy or the house is messy, my mind jumps straight to “I must be doing something wrong.” I know it’s not fully my fault, yet the guilt keeps popping up.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

A lot of the time. My heart’s been racing over little stuff—like whether I’m holding him “correctly” or if the milk is warm enough—without any real reason. It’s hard to turn those worries off, even when everything looks safe.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes—sometimes it hits out of nowhere. My chest gets tight, the room feels too loud, and I’m suddenly convinced the baby’s too quiet—even when he’s right there breathing fine. It passes, but it’s scary when it happens.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, honestly. Feels like chores, feedings, texts pile up faster than I can clear them. I start one task and three more appear—by evening I’m staring at the mess wondering how everyone else keeps afloat.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes. I lie down exhausted, then lie awake replaying tiny mistakes or tomorrow’s “what-ifs.” I drift off eventually, but I wake a couple of times—sometimes with tears on my face—and it takes ages to settle again.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… pretty much every day. It’s like a gray cloud that settles as soon as I open my eyes. I can still smile for the baby, but inside I just feel heavy and weepy, and some mornings it’s hard to get out of bed.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
A couple of nights this week. It’s usually once the baby’s finally down and the house is quiet—everything catches up and the tears just leak out. I try to keep it soft so I won’t wake anyone.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
It’s fluttered through my mind—like a quick flash that I should disappear—but that’s all. I’m scared of it, so I’d never act; I’ve got no plan, no means, and I would tell someone if it got stronger.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 23: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note

**Symptoms endorsed**  
- Persistent low mood, daily tearfulness, anhedonia (Q2, Q8, Q9)  
- Sleep disruption clearly linked to ruminating worries/sadness (Q7)  
- Excessive guilt / self-blame regarding infant care (Q3)  
- Marked generalized anxiety, "racing heart," situational panic episodes (Q4, Q5)  
- Subjective sense of being overwhelmed and unable to cope with daily tasks (Q6)  

**Observed patterns**  
Symptom onset post-delivery, present most days, interfere with functioning and enjoyment of motherhood. No current psychotic features; insight intact.

**Safety flag**  
Passive suicidal ideation ("should disappear") reported but no plan, intent, or preparatory behavior; patient verbalizes willingness to alert supports if thoughts worsen.

**Screening significance**  
Score pattern and clinical descriptors are consistent with moderate-to-severe postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety; formal diagnostic interview and safety plan recommended.
